blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face elevated danger, amid an unusual transition. Historically this was among the world's most dangerous places for trans women (with a documented life expectancy of 35 years; the killing of a trans woman who had been deported from the country where she sought asylum became the first hate-motivated homicide prosecution of its kind). Since 2022, the head of state's gang crackdown has collapsed the national homicide rate by ~98% (107 to 1.9 per 100k), dramatically reducing the gang violence that drove much anti-trans predation.

The trade-off is a state of exception with mass arbitrary detention (75,000+ imprisoned, minimal due process) — a risk mechanism that falls on anyone police decide to target, including gender-nonconforming people, with no effective recourse. There is no legal gender recognition law (administrative name change only), no SOGI hate-crime statute, and no institutional protection infrastructure.
blindOutOfScope: The state of exception affects all travellers; its trans-specific application is a risk mechanism, not a documented pattern.
blindSourceSummaries: A foreign-policy magazine piece (Mar 2020): this country's justice system takes on a historic case after the death of a transgender asylum seeker could yield its first hate-crime homicide conviction.
NOTE: this regional crime-analysis article is about the world region's homicide rates generally, not this country's LGBT situation specifically; included as general security context.
Academic article (2024): profile of homicides against LGBTI+ people in this country (2000-2020) - builds a profile of crimes, victims and perpetrators of anti-LGBTI+ homicides over two decades.

International human-rights organisation report (Oct 2020): violence and discrimination against LGBT people in this country and two neighbouring states, and obstacles to asylum in a wealthier destination country - opens with the story of a 29-year-old trans woman who fled abroad and was later killed back home.

International human-rights organisation report (Jan 2021): violence and discrimination against LGBT people in this country - full report with recommendations to the president, attorney general, congress and ministries.

International human-rights organisation (July 2020): three police officers convicted in this country for the killing of the trans woman whose story opened the October report - a rare case of accountability for anti-trans violence.
LGBT community newspaper (Sept 2015): this country's lawmakers approved enhanced hate-crime penalties covering crimes motivated by the victim's sexual orientation or gender identity.
blindLocalsOnly: The administrative name-change-only process and the absent legal-gender-recognition law are resident-facing; the historical life-expectancy figure and the landmark prosecuted killing describe residents.
